stories.notes: Story has zero acceptance criteria and describes a complex multi-platform live preview feature across GO, UP, MX in a CMS. Openspec must run first to elaborate requirements, define ACs, and add technical depth. Speckit then hardens with testability criteria, security checks, and edge cases. Spec is null and ACs are empty, confirming no prior hand-curation.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — live preview does not exist in the codebase. Attachment point is useContent/ContentstackContext which all 236+ content consumers depend on. VerificationCriteria derived from the description's concrete testable behaviour ('reflects changes immediately without full page reload or republish'). VCs stop at our boundary since contentstack.io is unreachable at test time.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria with a valuable note about the boundary (useContent/ContentstackContext) and test-time constraints (contentstack.io unreachable). I created all ACs from the story title/description and openspec's note. Key design decisions: (1) Every AC stops at our boundary — we verify what our code renders/receives, not what contentstack.io does internally, consistent with openspec's boundary note. (2) AC-1/AC-2 directly encode the story's concrete testable behaviour ('reflects changes immediately without full page reload or republish'). (3) AC-3 ensures surgical re-renders, not brute-force page refresh. (4) AC-4/AC-10/AC-12 cover session lifecycle (start, end, reconnect, absent). (5) AC-5/AC-6/AC-7/AC-8 cover error handling and resilience (disconnect, reconnect, malformed data, burst). (6) AC-9 addresses security isolation of preview from production. (7) AC-11 addresses cleanup/resource leaks. (8) AC-13 addresses the multi-locale scope (GO, UP, MX) from the story title. I could not review actual source files for useContent/ContentstackContext — if those files contain existing error-handling patterns or context shapes that should constrain these ACs, a follow-up review with file access would strengthen them.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Speckit carried the majority of the spec workload: it authored all 13 acceptance criteria from scratch while openspec contributed only boundary/context notes without producing any ACs (acceptanceChanged: false, splitCount: 0). This is a role inversion — openspec was assigned to elaborate requirements and define ACs first, but left that work entirely to speckit. The resulting AC coverage described in speckit's notes (session lifecycle, error/resilience, security isolation, cleanup, multi-locale scope) appears comprehensive and well-reasoned, but the story's acceptanceCriteria array is still empty in the provided data, meaning the ACs may not have been persisted to the story object. Additionally, no story splits were proposed despite this being a complex multi-platform (GO, UP, MX) live-preview feature touching 236+ content consumers — at minimum a split into preview-session-management vs preview-rendering-pipeline would be advisable. Speckit also flagged it could not access source files for useContent/ContentstackContext, so the ACs are unconstrained by existing code patterns. Human review should: (1) verify ACs were actually written to the story, (2) confirm openspec's boundary analysis against real source, (3) evaluate whether the story should be split, (4) validate that 13 ACs for a single story are not too broad for one implementation pass.
